summary: Practise Python data cleaning, statistical analysis and visualization. Build reproducible outputs for your reporting workflow. Explore the course.
lede: Quantitative analysis using Python helps data analysts, research officers and monitoring specialists prepare numerical data and produce reproducible findings. Participants practise checking and cleaning datasets, calculating descriptive summaries, and selecting and interpreting statistical tests, with an introductory look at regression diagnostics. They also create charts and document decisions in Jupyter notebooks that colleagues can rerun, making results easier to inspect and communicate.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who already work with numerical data and need to analyse it in Python, check their methods and communicate findings with clear statistical and visual evidence.
prerequisites: You should have basic Python coding experience, including variables, lists, functions and running scripts or notebooks. Bring a laptop with Python and Jupyter installed, plus pandas, NumPy, SciPy, statsmodels, Matplotlib and Seaborn. Use a non-confidential CSV you are permitted to analyse; no programming background beyond introductory Python is assumed.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
Data science & machine learning in practice
